summary: Charles Norman Seddon was an Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Balliol College, Oxford (1889–1891). In 1924, he was appointed Reader in Persian and Marathi at the University of Oxford.
Charles Oman was a historian and archaeologist who studied at New College from circa 1878 to 1882. He held a post at the University of Oxford from circa 1883 to 1946.

Charles Otto Blagden worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Dulwich College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (circa 1883–1886), and later served at SOAS University of London from circa 1917 to 1935.

An Indologist and linguist, Brown studied at the East India Company College and under traditional teachers Kodandarama Panthulu, Tippabhatla, and Vatthyam. He served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1817–1855) and as Professor of Telugu at UCL (circa 1865–1879).
Charles Picard was a scholar in history and archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Lyon from circa 1919 to 1934 and at the University of Paris from circa 1934 to 1955.

Charles Ramble works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Durham and Oxford, where he was taught by Michael Aris. His posts include professor at Oxford (2002–2005) and Director of Studies at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2009).

Charles Rieu worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Humbert, Lassen, Freytag, and Gildemeister, earning a doctorate at Bonn. He served at the British Museum, UCL, and Cambridge.

Charles Robert Wilson worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the City of London School, Wadham College, and Oxford (D.Litt. by 1902), later serving in the Bengal Education Department and as Principal of Patna College (circa 1900–1902).

Charles Rockwell Lanman was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Yale under Whitney and Hadley, and in Germany under Weber, Roth, Curtius, and Leskien. He taught at Johns Hopkins (1876–1880) and served as a professor at Harvard (1880–1926).

Charles S. Prebish is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Case Western Reserve University and under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He spent much of his career at Pennsylvania State University (circa 1972–2007).

Charles Schoebel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Eugène Burnouf. In 1845, he held teaching posts in German at both Lycée de Reims and Collège Sainte-Barbe.

Charles Swynnerton was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at University College London and earned an M.A. from the University of Oxford. He served as Headmaster of Ramsey Grammar School.

Charles Taliaferro is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College, the University of Rhode Island, Harvard Divinity School, and Brown University, and served as a professor at St. Olaf College from circa 1985 to 2022.

Charles Taylor is a philosopher who studied at Selwyn House School, McGill University, and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at Université de Montréal (circa 1961–1971), McGill University (circa 1961–1998), and Northwestern University (circa 2002).

Charles Ulysse Renel was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École Normale Supérieure, and the University of Lyon under Paul Regnaud. He held posts at the universities of Caen, Franche-Comté, and Lyon.

Charles Wei-hsun Fu worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at National Taiwan University (circa 1952–1956) and the University of Illinois System (circa 1965–1969), and held a post at Ohio University (circa 1969–1972).

Charles Wilkins was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kālinātha. He served as librarian for the East India Company and the India Office Library, and was an examiner of Oriental languages at the East India Company College and Addiscombe Military Seminary.
Charles Willemen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied under William Reynolds Beal Acker. He held an academic post as professor at Ghent University, attested from 1999 to 2001.

De Harlez de Deulin studied law at the University of Liège before working in Iranian, Central Asian, Sinological, and Indological studies. He served as director of Collège Saint-Quirin and was appointed professor of Sanskrit and Oriental studies at KU Leuven in 1871.

Charlotte Krause was an Indologist who studied at Marburg, Tübingen, Berlin, and Leipzig, working under Ernst Windisch, Richard von Garbe, Johannes Hertel, and Vijaya Indra Suri. She was Hertel's assistant at Leipzig and later Curator at Scindia Oriental Institute (1942–1947).
